the ACR AppropriatenESS Criteria® are evidence-based guidelines to assist referring physicians and radiologists in making the right imaging decision at the right time for each patient: to guide ordering of appropriate imaging exams, reducing unnecessary radiation and contrast exposure to patients as well as providing the optimal study for diagnosis and treatment of their ailments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are no evidence-based recommendations for the use of imaging modalities in the follow-up of patients after resection of malignant musculoskeletal tumors.
the use of imaging for follow-up of musculoskeletal tumors is not standardized and varies widely among institutions and among individual physicians.

the ACR AppropriatenESS Criteria are evidence-based and expert-driven guidelines that are intended to assist referring physicians and other members of the medical team in clinical decision-making about appropriate imaging examinations.
